first.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot: competitor pricing erosion, falling activation, and falling onboarding completion. Promotional pricing (memory_73) most directly counters the competitor threat, but it targets price-sensitive SMB accounts specifically and risks attracting lower-margin, less durable revenue—directly at odds with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I flag that risk rather than act on it this cycle. Onboarding completion is down 4% and two independent archived records (memory_31, memory_86) show durable activation gains from simplifying onboarding, making it the more controllable, internally-validated lever that also plausibly helps the 6% activation decline (onboarding and activation are adjacent in the funnel). I verified memory_31 to confirm the onboarding-simplification evidence is robust (not just correlational) and verified memory_73 to check whether the promotional pricing record shows any longer-term retention/quality caveats before ruling it out. Given only one test slot, I'm prioritizing fixing our own funnel decay over reacting to competitor pricing, since a pricing war response is riskier and harder to reverse than a UX fix. I'm treating this as a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout since we haven't re-verified current segment conditions post-competitor-entry, and I'm preserving uncertainty about whether onboarding fixes alone will offset both activation and competitive pressure.
